gaps.concept: Type 1 diabetes requires basal and mealtime insulin because autoimmune beta-cell loss leaves little or no endogenous insulin.
gaps.why_tested: A newly diagnosed patient with type 1 diabetes needs a drug regimen that replaces both background and meal-related insulin.

gaps.concept: Insulin activates a receptor tyrosine kinase, promoting GLUT4 translocation in muscle and adipose tissue.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks how injected insulin increases glucose uptake after a meal.

gaps.concept: Insulin drives potassium into cells through Na+/K+-ATPase activation and can cause hypokalemia.
gaps.why_tested: Serum potassium falls after insulin is given for hyperkalemia or diabetic ketoacidosis.

gaps.concept: Rapid-acting insulin covers meals; NPH has a pronounced peak; long-acting analogs provide flatter basal coverage.
gaps.why_tested: The timing of hypoglycemia after an insulin injection identifies the preparation.

gaps.concept: Glucagon treats severe hypoglycemia by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and is less effective when liver glycogen is depleted.
gaps.why_tested: A patient cannot swallow during a hypoglycemic episode, or fails to respond after prolonged fasting.

gaps.concept: Metformin activates AMPK, contributing to reduced hepatic gluconeogenesis.
gaps.why_tested: A mechanism question asks for the intracellular pathway targeted by a first-line diabetes drug.

gaps.concept: Sulfonylureas and meglitinides require functioning beta cells; short-acting meglitinides primarily control postprandial glucose.
gaps.why_tested: A meal-related glucose spike or absent endogenous insulin distinguishes a meglitinide from insulin therapy.

gaps.concept: Chlorpropamide can enhance antidiuretic hormone action and cause SIADH-like hyponatremia.
gaps.why_tested: An older patient taking a first-generation sulfonylurea develops low serum sodium.

gaps.concept: DPP-4 inhibitors can cause pancreatitis; saxagliptin is associated with increased heart-failure hospitalization.
gaps.why_tested: Abdominal pain or new heart failure follows initiation of a weight-neutral diabetes drug. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/022350s026lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors delay intestinal brush-border carbohydrate digestion, reducing postprandial hyperglycemia.
gaps.why_tested: A drug lowers glucose excursions after meals without stimulating insulin secretion. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/020482s027lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Pramlintide replaces beta-cell-derived amylin and can supplement mealtime insulin in type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
gaps.why_tested: A patient using mealtime insulin receives an additional injectable hormone analog. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2015/021332s025lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: SGLT2 inhibitors rarely cause Fournier gangrene, a necrotizing infection of the perineum.
gaps.why_tested: Perineal pain and systemic illness develop after a drug that causes glucosuria. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/204629s041lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Phentermine can cause tachycardia, hypertension, and insomnia; hyperthyroidism and cardiovascular disease argue against its use.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops adrenergic symptoms after starting an appetite suppressant. [Drug label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=315b8a94-b7cc-1b47-e063-6294a90a2d39)

gaps.concept: Topiramate in phentermine/topiramate increases fetal cleft-lip and cleft-palate risk.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient reports taking combination weight-loss medication early in gestation. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/022580s026lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Topiramate inhibits carbonic anhydrase and can cause metabolic acidosis and calcium-phosphate kidney stones.
gaps.why_tested: Low bicarbonate or nephrolithiasis follows phentermine/topiramate treatment. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/022580s031lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Bupropion stimulates hypothalamic POMC appetite pathways; naltrexone blocks opioid feedback that limits this stimulation.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks how the two components of a weight-loss combination suppress appetite.

gaps.concept: Naltrexone/bupropion can precipitate opioid withdrawal and increase seizure risk; avoid it with chronic opioid use or seizure disorders.
gaps.why_tested: A patient taking opioids or with a seizure history is considered for appetite suppression. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/200063s020lbl.pdf)

gaps.concept: Insulin does not cross the placenta and is a standard pharmacologic choice for gestational diabetes.
gaps.why_tested: Persistent hyperglycemia in pregnancy prompts selection of a fetal-safe glucose-lowering drug.
